text:
Priya (eng-platform): quick check — we need a concrete plan to correlate route-level SLOs (P50/P95/P99, TTFT, tokens/sec) with runtime/emitter tags so console panels can show per-model and per-route breakdowns. who owns the emitter changes?
Marco (eng-runtime): we can add route_id + model_variant as tags on the runtime emitter. cost question: high-cardinality if we do variant+route across all services. recommend sampling and pre-aggregation.
Jordan (eng-sre): agree on sampling. also need quotas on metric ingest to avoid billing spike. propose 1% sampling for high-volume routes, 100% for routes flagged as "critical".
Priya (eng-platform): that sounds reasonable. curious about TTFT semantics — do we record TTFT at request-level (first token latency) and also p99 on tokens/sec?
Marco (eng-runtime): yes: emit two metrics: `route.ttft_ms` (histogram) and `route.tokens_per_sec` (gauge/sec windowed avg). TTFT as timer, tokens/sec as a sampled gauge every 10s. For histograms use HDR or prometheus summaries — we already support HDR in pipeline.
Ben (console): for charts we'll need precomputed P50/P95/P99 and an aggregated TTFT heatmap per route/model. console can display either model-focused or route-focused views — need contracts on label names (`route`, `route_id`, `model`, `model_variant`, `region`).
Ava (product): also surface rolling-degradation UX — when a model's p95 spikes, show fallback route and recent rollout tag. can we emit `rollout_id` or `canary=true`?
Marco (eng-runtime): we can emit `rollout_id` or `canary=1` on requests that hit new variants. downside: increases label cardinality; suggest `rollout_id` only for canary buckets (small cardinality) + aggregate tag `is_canary` boolean.
Jordan (eng-sre): operational note: sampling must be deterministic by request-id so we can join traces and metrics if needed. also retention policy: keep high-res samples for 7 days, rollup to 1m for 90 days.
Priya (eng-platform): action items so we're aligned: 1) runtime: add tags `route_id`, `model`, `model_variant`, `region`, `is_canary`, `rollout_id` (only for canary) and emit `route.ttft_ms` histogram + `route.tokens_per_sec` gauge. 2) runtime: implement deterministic sampling 1% for high-volume routes, 100% for critical. 3) metrics infra: pre-aggregate p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec windows. 4) console: new panels — p50/p95/p99 latency, TTFT heatmap, tokens/sec timeseries, and a correlation view between rollouts and p95.
Ben (console): noted. I also want a compact per-route card showing current p95, delta vs baseline, and a quick link to recent canary rollouts. will mock and share.
Marco (eng-runtime): sample emitter config snippet below — this is what I'd add to runtime.
```
# emitter config (pseudo)
emitter.tags = ["route_id","model","model_variant","region","is_canary"]
emitter.ttft.histogram = true
emitter.tokens.gauge_window = 10s
emitter.sampling.rule("high_volume", rate=0.01, match="route_volume>1k")
emitter.sampling.rule("critical", rate=1.0, match="route in critical_routes")
```
Jordan (eng-sre): fine but add quota enforcement on metric ingestion per team to avoid runaway costs. also add alerting SLI: when p95 increases >30% vs baseline for 5m, create incident-priority P2.
Ava (product): for rollout UX, can we show a small timeline that overlays `is_canary` periods on the latency chart? engineers should be able to filter to only canary vs baseline.
Priya (eng-platform): yes. UX and panel specs due EOD Wed. runtime to PR emitter changes by Thu. infra to confirm pre-aggregation SLA and cost estimate by next Tue. 30-min sync tomorrow 11:30am to iron out sampling rules.
Ben (console): I'll post a quick mock before the sync.
Marco (eng-runtime): will start branch; will ping when config is up for review.
ops-bot: Reminder — 30-minute sync scheduled for 11:30 AM tomorrow in #eng-platform. :bell:
Priya (eng-platform): thanks all — keeping this tight since product wants per-route SLOs in the console for next release.
